accuracy.evidence: Checked against the GCSE Mathematics subject content (DfE 2013: apply trigonometric ratios to find angles and lengths in right-angled triangles in 2D) and CCSS HSG-SRT.C.8, with angles of elevation and depression defined from the horizontal as in standard GCSE texts. Every number recomputed with Math.tan/sin: atan(12.5/20) = 32.0°; 40/tan 20° = 109.9 m so the boat at 110 m reads 20.0°; 20 × tan 35° = 14.0 m, plus 1.6 m = 15.6 m; 50/tan 12° = 235.2 m, 50 × tan 12° = 10.6 m, 50/sin 12° = 240.5 m, 50/tan 78° = 10.6 m; challenge values 25.2, 19.3, 35.8, 28.7, 35.0, 41.0, 15.9, 14.4, 12.9, 298.6, 21.4 and 309.1 m. Parameterised answers (a, h + 1.5, 90 − a, h) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors listed in examiner reports for GCSE trigonometry questions and in Blackett & Tall (1991): measuring the angle from the vertical (90° − θ), naming sides from the right angle instead of the given angle, choosing sin when the hypotenuse is unknown, multiplying by tan when the distance needs division, forgetting the observer's eye height, and giving the sight line (hypotenuse) when the ground distance is asked. Each has its own feedback in the lab and the challenge.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed; the highest 6-token Jaccard is 9.1% (shared shell scaffolding with flag_altexp.js). 140 Why trigonometric ratios work (similar triangles) and 143 Exact trigonometric values have no applied context. Only this lab drags a sight line up a tree, drags a boat until a cliff's depression reads 20° while the boat's elevation matches, sets an eye height before choosing the total, and drags a boat to 12° from a lighthouse before choosing the distance calculation.

lab_teaches.evidence: Five tasks build the method in order: elevation is measured up from the horizontal; depression is measured down from the horizontal and equals the elevation from below (alternate angles); name sides from the angle and pick tan; add the eye height; divide by tan to find a distance. Angle readouts update live while dragging, so learners see the angle shrink as the boat moves out before they are told.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'The vertical tree, down to the line of sight', '70°' for the elevation that matches a 20° depression, '14.0 m' (no eye height) for the tree, and 'It gets bigger' for a boat sailing away. The drags and readouts then disprove each one.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions (tower, cliff and boat, definition, kite string, building with eye height, tower and car), each with two tagged wrong answers: wrongRatio, flip, vertical, straight, updown, eye and hyp. Each tag has its own message, e.g. 'Dividing by sin gives the sloping sight line. The ground distance is the adjacent side: 80 ÷ tan 15°.'

readability.evidence: Kid explanation Flesch-Kincaid grade 3.9 (limit 6.5) and adult 6.7 (limit 9.5), checked with learn/readability.py. The terms horizontal, line of sight, opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse are each explained in a plain sentence where they first appear, and each worked example (35° tree, 12° lighthouse) gives the full calculation.

no_filler.evidence: No filler patterns matched. Each kid paragraph covers one step: the definitions, equal alternate angles, choosing the ratio, eye height and distances. The adult text gives curriculum links, the lab sequence and named errors. Explanation overlap with every other lesson is at most 0.2%.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px and 1200 px (light and dark) for every step before and after Show me: the scenes are drawn to true scale so the angles are honest, labels avoid the canopy (the 14.0 m label moved below it), and the ratio tiles shrink their font to fit three across at 360 px. The lighthouse calculation tiles sit above the feedback footer, and drag handles have a 26–30 px reach.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag and tap has a button twin: aim up/down 0.5 m, boat ◀/▶ 1 m, 10 m (5 m, 25 m at the lighthouse), side-naming buttons, ratio, total-height and distance buttons, eye height up/down 0.1 m. The canvas aria-label states the distances, heights and current angle after each action. walk.cjs: axe clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13, no console errors.
